# GoPatina

> GoPatina is an open-source Go toolchain front end in which ordinary Go code can opt into running the way Rust code does: no garbage collector, ownership and borrowing, and Rust-grade memory safety. Without a flag it runs the installed Go toolchain unchanged. It is an experiment by Pigfox to get Go developers past Rust's learning curve.

Status: early. Phase 1 works for a defined subset of Go; real programs need features still in progress. Default mode works for all Go. For the phase 1 subset (functions, structs and methods, every integer type, float32 and float64, named types such as type Op int with their methods, type aliases, slices, strings, errors, fmt printing, and read-only s[i:] suffix arguments), -emit-rust, -patina, -patina=check, -explain and gopatina verify are implemented, checked by differential tests (101 golden programs, 23 rejection fixtures and 3 Go-only semantics cases; same stdout, first stderr line and exit status as Go's reference build, go build -gcflags=all=-N -l) and byte-identical rebuilds. Not supported yet: goroutines and channels, maps, closures, interfaces, generics, defer, general slicing, slices with high or max bounds, saved slice views, most of the standard library. Two bars. Speed: equivalent to hand-written Rust within ±0.5%, by a two one-sided tests (TOST) equivalence test at 5 sigma (one-sided p ~ 2.9e-7 per bound). Correctness (Six Sigma): at most 3.4 defects per million, shown at 6 sigma confidence by 0 defects in at least 6,099,050 differential tests against Go (one-sided alpha ~ 9.9e-10); the milestone, 881,098 defect-free tests, shows the same rate at 95% confidence (rule of three). Speed bar status (2026-11-22, test server, CPU counters, rustc 1.100.0 for both): met on user instructions, the primary metric, at 5 and 6 sigma (fib 1.0000082, sieve 1.0000062, suffix-sum 1.0000071, all equivalent); run time not yet decided (measured under load). The correctness bar is pending. Earlier local results (2026-11-21, laptop, not official): fib and suffix-sum execute the same instructions as hand-written Rust to within 0.0003%; sieve measured 1.30x the instructions and about 7% slower, and RFC 0006 loop specialization has since removed the cause, so its hot loop compiles to the same machine code; 1,318 generated development tests, 0 defects (far below the bar). The evidence page is structured as a report: hypotheses, method, apparatus, statistical analysis, results, threats to validity, reproducibility, references. Details in BENCHMARKS.md and docs/QUALITY.md. Last updated 2026-11-22.

## Docs

- [README](https://github.com/pigfox/gopatina#readme): project overview, status and quick start
- [Examples](https://github.com/pigfox/gopatina/blob/main/EXAMPLES.md): the three build modes on three small programs, with real and planned output labelled
- [Phase 1 subset](https://github.com/pigfox/gopatina/blob/main/docs/patina-subset.md): the Go the patina modes accept today
- [Feature matrix](https://github.com/pigfox/gopatina/blob/main/docs/compat.md): supported and planned Go features
- [Go-Rust disconnects](https://github.com/pigfox/gopatina/blob/main/docs/go-rust-disconnects.md): where Go and Rust semantics differ
- [RFC 0001](https://github.com/pigfox/gopatina/blob/main/docs/rfcs/0001-gopatina.md): the design, the GoPatina borrow checker, Rust underneath, deployment
- [RFC 0002](https://github.com/pigfox/gopatina/blob/main/docs/rfcs/0002-concurrency.md): goroutines on a multi-threaded async runtime
- [RFC 0003](https://github.com/pigfox/gopatina/blob/main/docs/rfcs/0003-toolchain-compatibility.md): toolchain compatibility and versioning
- [RFC 0004](https://github.com/pigfox/gopatina/blob/main/docs/rfcs/0004-read-only-slice-suffix.md): read-only slice suffix arguments
- [RFC 0005](https://github.com/pigfox/gopatina/blob/main/docs/rfcs/0005-phase1-semantic-exactness.md): phase 1 semantic exactness fixes
- [RFC 0006](https://github.com/pigfox/gopatina/blob/main/docs/rfcs/0006-proven-ranges.md): proven integer ranges and loop specialization
- [The two bars](https://github.com/pigfox/gopatina/blob/main/docs/QUALITY.md#the-two-bars): the speed and correctness bars with their hypotheses and formulas
- [Benchmarks](https://github.com/pigfox/gopatina/blob/main/BENCHMARKS.md): local measurements with raw results and caveats; official results will be published there
